findings.title: Watch job can append model output to any repo file via '..' in the merge target
findings.why: save_intent accepts ctl['into'] when it starts with 'intent/auto/' and (ROOT / into).is_file(). It never resolves the path, so a value like 'intent/auto/../../CLAUDE.md', 'intent/auto/../../app/app.js' or 'intent/auto/../../.claude/hooks/no-self-approve.py' passes both checks. watch.py then appends the agent's free text to that file. The model's reply depends on untrusted evidence in its prompt and tools (CI logs, failing test names, commit subjects, metric data). A prompt injection planted there can therefore make the level-2 agent, which is meant to have read tools only, write into app code, hooks or CLAUDE.md. The write is done by watch.py itself, so the Claude Code hooks (protect-paths, no-self-approve) never see it.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the path and require it to be a direct child of AUTO: f = (ROOT / into).resolve(); accept only if f.parent == AUTO.resolve() and f.suffix == '.md' and f.name in {p.name for p, _, _ in open_intents()}. Otherwise treat the reply as 'new'. Add a test with an 'intent/auto/../../x' target.
findings.fingerprint: scripts/watch.py|CWE-22|watch job can append model output to any

findings.title: 'Read-only' allowlist Bash(git diff:*)/git log/git show lets the agent write files through --output
findings.why: review.py (line 19), triage.py (line 12) and scan.py (line 20) present 'Bash(git diff:*)', 'Bash(git log:*)' and 'Bash(git show:*)' as read-only. Each of these git commands takes --output=<file>, which writes to an arbitrary path. They also honour diff drivers and textconv set in the repo config. The reviewer reads a diff and PR.md written by another agent, and triage reads build logs. Both are untrusted inputs that can carry instructions. The prefix rule matches any arguments, so a session meant to be read-only can overwrite files in the worktree, in the main checkout (an absolute path) or in the home directory.
findings.suggestion: Narrow the rules or drop them in favour of Read/Grep plus a wrapper script that runs fixed git commands, for example a scripts/git-ro.py that rejects --output, --ext-diff and --textconv. Alternatively, add a PreToolUse hook that denies git diff/log/show calls containing '--output' or '--ext-diff'. Apply the same fix to the level-2 tools in ops/bands.yaml if they use these rules.
findings.fingerprint: scripts/review.py|CWE-73|read only allowlist bash git diff git lo

findings.title: Deploy MCP passes the agent-supplied 'ref' to git without '--' or validation
findings.why: The ref argument of deploy and prepare_release goes straight to 'git rev-parse --short=7 <ref>' and 'git archive --format=tar <ref> app' in scripts/deploy.py (lines 56 and 60), with no '--' before it and no check of its shape. A ref that starts with '-' is parsed as an option. git archive has --output=<file> (a file write) and --remote=<url> (a network fetch). The 'ref' is chosen by the agent, and the agent may be steered by untrusted evidence on watch runs. This tool is the scope boundary that is meant to hold whatever the agent does.
findings.suggestion: In server.py, reject any ref that does not match ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ or that starts with '-'. In deploy.build, resolve it once with 'git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}' and pass only the resolved full sha to git archive.
findings.fingerprint: tools/deploy-mcp/server.py|CWE-88|deploy mcp passes the agent supplied ref

findings.title: Spec job treats 'Status: accepted' anywhere in the intent as approval
findings.why: The pattern '^.*Status:[[:space:]]*accepted' matches the text anywhere on any line, not only the intent's own status line. An intent that quotes a ticket, a prior decision or a template line such as '(set Status: accepted to approve)' starts the headless /write-spec job on its first commit while it is still a draft. That job then commits a spec on main. The approval rule in CLAUDE.md says that only a person setting the status starts the next step. Separately, '$(git diff-tree …)' word-splits file names that contain spaces.
findings.suggestion: Match only the header line, for example grep -qE '^Status:[[:space:]]*accepted[[:space:]]*$' (or the template's exact line). Read file names with 'git diff-tree -z … | while IFS= read -r -d '' f'.
findings.fingerprint: scripts/on-intent-accepted.sh|other|spec job treats status accepted anywhere
